subject: Request: Match funding + trial extension for longitudinal biodata pilot
messages:
From: Dr. Emily Santos <e.santos@openlab.edu>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: sustained-credit support for longitudinal biodata pilot

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last month — the latency profiles you showed look promising for our near-real-time de-identification pipeline. Our team at OpenLab is preparing a longitudinal biodata study spanning MRI and wearable sensor data for 18 months. We submitted a brief protocol summary (attached) and have two asks:

1) A promotional credit top-up to cover an initial 90-day window (we estimate ~$9k of Redwood usage for preprocessing + embeddings).
2) A trial-extension for the hosted sandbox from the standard 30 days to 90 days so our IRB and computing workflows can complete staging.

We are a non-profit research unit and would be extremely grateful for a credit match — we can commit to a pilot case study and a co-authored methods note if that helps. Please let me know what information you need (budget codes, PO, or sign-off language).

Attachments: protocol_summary.pdf (1 page)

Best,
Emily
Dr. Emily Santos
Senior Research Scientist, OpenLab University
Email: e.santos@openlab.edu
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Santos <e.santos@openlab.edu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: sustained-credit support for longitudinal biodata pilot

Hi Emily — thanks for the note and for the attached protocol. This is the sort of reproducible research we like supporting. Quick responses to set expectations:

- We can put together a discretionary credit match for non-profit academic pilots; approvals typically take 48–72 hours once Grants has the protocol and estimated usage.
- For trial extensions, we usually approve up to 90 days for studies with IRB timelines; we need a short statement confirming no PHI will be sent and that data will be de-identified.

Next steps I can kick off today: I will loop in Marissa (Academic Programs) and Priyom (partnering/grants coordination). Marissa — can you confirm whether a $9k top-up + 90-day sandbox extension is within discretionary limits, and if you need a PO or a signed credit agreement?

Emily — if you could reply to this thread with the IRB reference number (if available) and the lead PI name, that will help speed approvals. Also linking a short form we use for credit review: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf_example_credit_form/viewform

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Apr 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: sustained-credit support for longitudinal biodata pilot

Marissa, Priyom — forwarding Emily's ask. Summary: OpenLab (non-profit research unit) requests a $9k promotional credit top-up and a 90-day sandbox extension for an IRB-backed longitudinal biodata pilot (MRI + wearables). Attached is a 1-page protocol.

Why I think we should approve:
- High likelihood of publishable results and a methods note co-authorship, which aligns with academic outreach goals.
- Reasonable usage profile (compute + embeddings) and limited data residency concerns — they commit to de-identification up front.
- Good reference opportunity for a university lab with national collaborators.

Questions for approvals:
- Marissa: discretionary cap? Do we need a signed credit agreement or PO for $9k?
- Priyom: any precedent deals we should mirror on terms (attribution, co-authorship ask)?

I propose a conditional approval: 75% of requested credits up-front ($6,750) + 90-day sandbox; remaining 25% released after receipt of the IRB reference and a short postmortem plan (we can ask for a one-page deliverable).

Thanks — Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Santos <e.santos@openlab.edu>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 14:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: sustained-credit support for longitudinal biodata pilot

Hi Emily — pleasure to e-meet. After reviewing the protocol and Ben's recommendation, we are able to approve a promotional credit match under the Academic Pilot program with the following conditions: 

1) An initial credit allocation of $6,750 will be applied to your sandbox account immediately. We can provision an additional $2,250 upon receipt of either an IRB reference number or a short confirmation from your PI that all data will be de-identified and within the scope described.

2) We will extend your hosted sandbox trial to 90 days from the date of the extension approval (sandbox activation details to follow).

3) We require a one-page post-pilot methods summary within 30 days of the pilot completion that we may reference in aggregate case studies. Redwood will not request identifiable data.

4) Please review and sign the attached credit_agreement.docx (standard academic credit terms) or provide a PO; for non-US universities we sometimes require a W-8/W-9 equivalent — our operations team will advise if needed.

If that works, please reply with the IRB number (or PI confirmation) and whether you prefer DocuSign or an emailed PO. I'll have Operations send the DocuSign link as soon as you confirm.

Warm regards,
Marissa Cole
Head, Academic Programs | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: credit_agreement.docx

On a related note, Priyom — thanks for the input on attribution; we should offer co-authorship as a goodwill gesture when it is warranted, but not as a contractual requirement.
